papers.title: Data-driven reassessment of lattice matching in ScAlN/GaN heterostructures grown by sputter epitaxy and molecular beam epitaxy
papers.summary: We reassessed the lattice-matching behavior of ScAlN thin films grown on GaN by constructing a unified dataset from sputter epitaxy, molecular beam epitaxy (MBE), and literature reports. The dataset comprised 197 samples, including 32 MBE-grown and 70 sputter-grown films from our laboratories and 95 literature data points, for which Sc composition, growth temperature, film thickness, polarity, growth technique, and a- and c-axis lattice constants were compiled. The compiled data were analyzed using a neural-network-based surrogate model to extract smooth lattice-constant trends within the experimentally covered parameter range, and these trends were subsequently parameterized by empirical polynomial functions of Sc composition and growth temperature. The lattice-matched Sc composition of ScxAl1−xN to GaN was estimated to be x ≈ 0.10–0.13, which is lower than the conventional value of approximately 0.18 and is only weakly dependent on growth temperature and growth technique. In contrast, the c-axis lattice constant was strongly dependent on growth temperature and decreased at higher growth temperatures. This c-axis contraction, together with the reduced c/a ratio, is consistent with growth-temperature-dependent bond softening and local structural distortion in ScAlN, providing a possible structural link to polarization switching in ferroelectric nitrides.

papers.title: Investigation of single-event burnout mechanism in p-GaN gate HEMTs
papers.summary: In this work, the mechanism of single-event burnout (SEB) in p-GaN gate HEMTs is thoroughly investigated by irradiation experiments and simulations. The samples were irradiated with tantalum (Ta) ions (67 MeV cm2/mg in GaN). There are two distinct failure modes observed in samples occurring in SEB. One is the four-terminal short-circuit mode, and the other is the vertical short-circuit mode between the drain and the substrate. By comparing damaged structures, it can be inferred that both failure modes probably originated from the burnout of the drain. According to the transient currents and temperature distributions by simulations, it is found that the most sensitive region to SEB is the edge of the drain, rather than the edge of the gate or field plate. The SEB mechanism can be explained as follows. A large number of generated holes accumulate at the GaN/AlN interface, while a large number of electrons will accumulate at the Si-Sub/AlN interface, leading to a high electric field in the AlN layer and in turn enhancing the impact ionization. Then the generated electrons will drift to the drain and concentrate around the drain, which produces high current density as well as a high electric field near the drain. Therefore, the lattice temperature there is quickly raised to trigger thermal runaway at the drain.

papers.title: Epitaxial integration of GaN $μ$-platelets and thin films on metallic TiN using a hybrid approach
papers.summary: We demonstrate the synthesis of epitaxial, self-organized GaN $μ$-platelets on metallic TiN thin films. To this end, we first nucleate self-assembled GaN nanowires with number densities between 0.01 to 300 $μm^{-2}$ by molecular beam epitaxy. Subsequent overgrowth of these seed nanowires by metal-organic vapor phase epitaxy yields GaN $μ$-platelets with corresponding number densities. The platelets exhibit N-polarity and form an ohmic contact to the metallic TiN substrate. By adjusting the growth conditions during the metal-organic vapor phase epitaxy, particularly the carrier gas and precursor ratio, the morphology of the GaN can be controlled across a broad range. Growth under N$_{2}$ carrier gas and with a 1:1 NH$_{3}$/trimethylgallium precursor flow ratio results in platelet ensembles with broad diameter and height distributions. In contrast, employing an N$_{2}$/H$_{2}$ carrier gas mixture promotes the formation of more homogeneous ensembles with narrower size distributions around a diameter of $\approx$2 $μm$. Finally, N-rich growth conditions under H$_{2}$ carrier gas enhance lateral growth, leading to the formation of coalesced GaN layers. GaN grown under these latter conditions exhibits strong near-band-edge emission, accompanied by only weak deep-level luminescence at room temperature.

papers.title: IGZO optoelectronic synaptic transistor for neuromorphic vision and motion tracking applications
papers.summary: Neuromorphic vision systems that integrate optical sensing, memory, and information processing are promising candidates for overcoming the energy and bandwidth limitations of conventional von Neumann architectures. Here, we report an indium gallium zinc oxide (IGZO) optoelectronic synaptic transistor for neuromorphic vision and motion tracking applications. The fabricated device exhibits excellent electrical performance, including a high on/off current ratio of ∼1.06 × 108, a low subthreshold swing of 110.58 mV/dec, and a field-effect mobility of 1.52 cm2 V−1 s−1. Under 405 nm optical stimulation, the transistor successfully emulates essential biological synaptic behaviors, including intensity- and time-dependent synaptic plasticity, paired-pulse facilitation, short-term to long-term memory transition, and learning-forgetting-relearning characteristics, while operating with a low energy consumption of approximately 6.75 pJ per synaptic event. Photoluminescence and x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analyses reveal that oxygen-vacancy-related defect states induce carrier trapping and persistent photoconductivity, providing the physical mechanism responsible for the observed optoelectronic synaptic behavior. To demonstrate its practical applicability, a hardware–software co-designed neuromorphic vision framework employing a 128 × 64 IGZO synaptic transistor array model experimentally calibrated using measured devices' optoelectronic characteristics was simulated for real-time motion detection and vehicle tracking. The proposed system achieved a pixel localization accuracy of 94.8% through hardware-aware spatiotemporal preprocessing, significantly reducing redundant data transmission and computational overhead. These results demonstrate the potential of IGZO optoelectronic synaptic transistors as an energy-efficient platform for intelligent visual perception, edge artificial intelligence, and next-generation in-sensor neuromorphic computing.

papers.title: Distilling an atomistic foundation model is all you need for large-scale molecular dynamics of semiconductor interfaces
papers.summary: State-of-the-art atomistic foundation models provide broadly transferable energy and force predictions, but their direct deployment in large-scale molecular dynamics remains computationally costly. Here we examine whether their knowledge can be distilled into compact potentials while retaining the physical responses of heterogeneous semiconductor interfaces. From 128 pretrained models spanning 22 model families, we select a fixed EquiformerV3 teacher and train atomic cluster expansion (ACE) and neuroevolution potential (NEP) students without target-specific teacher fine-tuning, with both simulation speed and accessible system size improved by several orders of magnitude relative to the teacher model. Matched training configurations and architectures enable direct comparisons with students trained on density-functional-theory (DFT) reference labels. For 79,920-atom BAs/GaN interfaces, direct distillation preserves termination-dependent thermal conductance and dominant spectral features, with conductance differing by at most 6.6% from DFT-trained counterparts. In 29,792-atom Cu/diamond specimens loaded at 500 K, tensile strength and loading work differ by 2.8% and 1.5%, respectively. Exploratory SiC/a-C/SiC simulations retain the principal thermal bottleneck and the direction of the annealing response. Furthermore, a four-model committee retrieves 42-56% of the highest-error teacher configurations with a 10% selection budget and improves high-error force fitting, but does not consistently improve downstream properties. These findings demonstrate that direct distillation can preserve key interfacial thermal and mechanical responses in compact interatomic potentials, opening a path towards large-scale, high-throughput simulations of heterogeneous interfaces.

papers.title: High-Throughput Surface Screening Reveals Energetically Competitive Low-Symmetry Facets in Wurtzite Semiconductors
papers.summary: Surfaces and interfaces govern the performance of wurtzite semiconductors in electronics, sensing, and solar-fuel conversion. To date, first-principles studies have focused mostly on high-symmetry low-index facets, owing to the computational cost and complexity of modelling low-symmetry high-index surfaces. In practice, however, surface formation energy is determined by the planar atomic density and the strength of the bonds severed upon cleavage, neither of which inherently excludes high-Miller-index surfaces from being energetically competitive. Here, we combine automated surface generation, machine-learning interatomic potential screening, and density functional theory to explore 226 clean, stoichiometric surface models of wurtzite GaN, LaN, and ZnO, spanning all Miller orientations with $|h|,|k|,|l| \le 3$ and their inequivalent terminations. We find that low-symmetry high-index prismatic facets are energetically competitive with respect to the conventional $m$- and $a$-planes: nine of the fifteen lowest-energy nonpolar surfaces are high-index, and the five best candidates of each compound lie within only 2.5-5.3% of the minimum surface energy. Hybrid-functional calculations reveal, however, that this energetic proximity does not translate into similar electronic alignment. In GaN, the two most stable surfaces differ by just 0.08 J m$^{-2}$ in formation energy but by almost 0.8 eV in vacuum-referenced band-edge positions, whereas in LaN the nearly degenerate $m$- and $a$-planes are separated by 0.16 eV. Wurtzite facets with similar formation energies may therefore exhibit very different ionization potentials and electron affinities. Our results enable the joint, systematic assessment of stability and band alignment across the facets that can actually occur in wurtzites, and provide a map of candidate surfaces for the rational design of related nanostructure and heterointerfaces.
